non_retroactivity.rule: the 23.353553 bps figure is a *posterior* economic evaluation at the account size we actually hold; the rejected strategies were judged against the frozen 23.7906 bps and must not be recalculated against a smaller toll

split.reading: the exchange fee is a published schedule (KNOWN); spread, slippage and size-driven impact are modelled terms (ESTIMATED) whose constants the frozen model itself labels ASSUMED/ESTIMATED rather than observed.  The fee share is quoted at the frozen 1,000 USD reference; at 200 USDT the same fee is 20 of 23.35 bps, i.e. a larger share of a smaller bill

economic_decision.reading: the long-horizon region clears the toll by a wide margin, so a mechanism there could *pay for itself*; that is an arithmetic statement about the venue's take, not evidence that any mechanism can take the move.  The three tested mechanisms produced no demonstrated gross edge, so the margin stays unclaimed.
economic_decision.remaining_question: whether any mechanism suited to a holding period of about a day and upwards can convert the available movement into net return — a question this gate does not answer and does not recommend answering by opening another campaign
economic_decision.rule: movement margin is sufficient at a horizon when the measured median absolute move is at least 5x the toll the strategy would pay to trade it
economic_decision.verdict_basis: the rule is applied to the profile under evaluation, the low-turnover long-horizon region; the short-horizon families are reported alongside and their failure is a finding about them, not a contradiction of this verdict

purpose: Consolidate and verify the economic viability evidence before any further discovery campaign is even discussed.

clock_skew.reading: local clock minus venue clock after removing half the round trip; every timestamp in this programme is therefore trustworthy to about a third of a second, which matters for latency reasoning and for nothing else

collection.authentication: none — public endpoints only; no API key, no signature, no private call

depth.reading: static L2 depth walk at the sampled instant: the market-order cost a taker of that size would face *if the book stayed still*.  The largest measured walk across the four instruments and both sides is 0.000000 bps at the account size and 0.169344 bps at a hundred times the account, i.e. the book absorbs our size inside its best price.  It is a snapshot estimate, not realised slippage: no order was sent and no fill was observed.

measured_now: depth-based impact estimate per order size
still_estimated: base slippage as a modelling constant: the measured depth walk at account scale is inside one tick, so this term is a conservative penalty rather than a depth effect
maker adverse selection and fill probability
unknown_and_stated: historical spread for any past period (no endpoint exists)

published_fees.applicable_spot_schedule: SRC-01 Binance Spot VIP0, 10 bps maker / 10 bps taker
published_fees.bnb_discount: POSSIBLE, not confirmed for our account

quote_changes.reading: how often the mid moved between consecutive observations of the same bounded window; a coarse proxy for quote volatility, not a signal

spread.caveat: one bounded window of a few seconds across four instruments is a spot reading, not a regime: it cannot certify a past period and does not replace a forward campaign
spread.like_for_like: the model's spread term is the round-trip cost (2 legs x half-spread), which equals the full bid/ask spread, so the comparison against the measured full spread is like for like
